step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture describes an automated migration factory from on-premises to AWS. I've identified the core components from the whiteboard: an on-premises environment, AWS Application Discovery Service, DynamoDB, an EC2 'Migration Factory' instance, a CloudEndure service, an EC2 'Hot Replica' target, and a final 'Target EC2' instance. External actors include the 'Migration Team' and 'Slack'. I've carefully mapped the visual arrows and the transcript's narrative to define the data and control flows, ensuring that transient artifacts like 'Bake AMI' and 'Shared AMI' are described as actions within edge notes, not as separate nodes, adhering to the parsimony principle.

graph.name: Versant's Automated Cloud Migration Factory
graph.notes: This architecture illustrates Versant's automated process for migrating on-premises servers to AWS, significantly reducing migration time from hours to minutes. It leverages AWS services like Application Discovery Service and DynamoDB, alongside CloudEndure for continuous replication and an EC2-based migration factory for orchestration.

nodes.name: On-Premises Data Center
nodes.notes: Source on-premises servers where applications reside and from which data is migrated to AWS.

nodes.name: AWS Application Discovery Service
nodes.notes: Installed with agents on on-premises servers, it gathers inbound/outbound TCP connections and performance utilization metrics to inform instance sizing in AWS.

nodes.name: Migration Metadata Database
nodes.notes: Stores operational metadata for migrations, including RTOs, RPOs, infrastructure/business owners, target AWS account details, subnet, IP addresses, and tags for EC2 instances.

nodes.name: Migration Factory EC2
nodes.notes: An EC2 instance acting as the central orchestration engine (migration factory). It integrates with various services via APIs to automate the migration workflow, triggered by Slack commands.

nodes.name: CloudEndure Replication Target EC2
nodes.notes: An EC2 instance in AWS where CloudEndure continuously replicates block-by-block data from the on-premises servers, acting as a 'hot replica'.

nodes.name: CloudEndure Live Migration Service
nodes.notes: A service (acquired by AWS) that provides continuous, block-level data replication from on-premises source servers to an AWS EC2 target.

nodes.name: Target EC2 Instance
nodes.notes: The final migrated EC2 instance launched in the specified target AWS account from the baked and shared AMI, configured with parameters from DynamoDB.

nodes.name: Slack
nodes.notes: An external communication platform used by the migration team to issue commands that trigger the migration factory.

nodes.name: Migration Team
nodes.notes: Internal staff responsible for initiating and managing the cloud migration process, inputting metadata and triggering workflows.

edges.notes: On-premises servers send metadata (TCP connections, performance) via installed agents to AWS Application Discovery Service.
CloudEndure agents on on-premises servers initiate continuous block-level data replication to the CloudEndure service.
CloudEndure service continuously replicates data to the EC2 Hot Replica instance in AWS.
Migration Team populates DynamoDB with operational and configuration metadata for target EC2 instances.
Migration Team issues a command (e.g., 'migrate server X') via Slack.
Slack command triggers an API call to the Migration Factory EC2 instance.
Migration Factory EC2 calls the Application Discovery Service API to retrieve TCP connection data for the server being migrated.
Migration Factory EC2 calls the CloudEndure API to stop the continuous data replication for the target server.
Migration Factory EC2 orchestrates the baking of an AMI from the EC2 Hot Replica data.
Migration Factory EC2 retrieves migration metadata (instance type, IP, tags, target account) from DynamoDB.
Migration Factory EC2 shares the baked AMI to the target account and launches the Target EC2 Instance using the retrieved metadata.
